newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chase for scarce Russian shares, shorting seen.
newsitem.headline: Chase for scarce Russian shares, shorting seen.

text.p: Last minute, pre-New Year demand in the half-closed Russian shares market pushed prices up sharply on Friday and Monday, dealers said, adding that they had seen some short-selling and end-of-year account padding.
Leading shares have led a two day rally that saw the Russian Trading System close at 197.94 on Monday, 2.2 percent higher over Friday and dealers said many prices rose 5-7 percent over the two days.
UES closed at $0.091 up from $0.088 on Friday and a Thursday low of $0.086.
LUKoil, which traded as low as $10.10 on Christmas Day, closed on Monday at $11.30 after $11.20 on Friday.
"If this were a normal day, this kind of demand would go unnoticed. But now there is nothing to be found," said Vladislav Leonchuk of ING Bank, adding that many dealers were shorting the market.
"There has to be some kind of correction."
Market turnover was $5.2 million on Monday and less on the previous two trading days. A $10 million trading day is generally considered extremely thin.
Most investors were seen trying to anticipate a January bull market and some traders said the market would avoid a post-holiday correction on hopes of substantial new funds.
But traders on Friday who noticed the same growth noted that a few banks appeared to be pushing up prices to book substantial end of year profits.
